A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SEA and VA-SafetyBench. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: V1 reports original safety-alignment experiments, VA-SafetyBench evaluations, embedding optimization measurements, and appendix analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds a style-control ablation with cosine-distance measurements and embedding visualizations.

M1.justification: Figure 7 revises the stated optimization inputs and targets: video style control changes from image-style wording to video genre, and audio style control asks about speaker characteristics. These are localized prompt revisions; the architecture, optimization loss, and alignment procedure remain unchanged. Rerunning the existing experiments is not documented.

E1.justification: The training datasets, safety scenarios, image/video/audio coverage, and general-capability benchmarks are retained. The new style-control analysis uses existing coverage rather than introducing another dataset or task.

E2.justification: New Table 11 evaluates SEA against a content-only variant labeled 'SEA without style control.' Existing benchmark and case-study comparator sets remain unchanged; 'sft_VLGuard2' is relabeled 'VLGuard,' not newly added.

E3.justification: Appendix B.3 adds a 3,000-example comparison with and without style control, using average cosine distance and t-SNE visualization. Benchmark scoring and alignment-training budgets are retained. The scenario sample sizes added to Tables 8–9 disclose existing settings rather than establish changed sample counts.

E4.justification: New Appendix B.3 tests whether style control increases embedding diversity through a removal ablation and visualizations across three models. This is a focused component analysis; the earlier optimization validation, temporal-versus-spatial stitching comparison, and three case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added cosine-distance averages and t-SNE plots do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Table 11 adds SEA versus no-style-control cosine distances: 0.03109 versus 0.03023 for LLaVA, 0.06986 versus 0.06663 for Qwen2-VL, and 0.00796 versus 0.00745 for Qwen2-Audio. Figure 8 adds qualitative distribution findings. Existing benchmark scores and case-study outcomes are unchanged.

T1.justification: The architecture formulation and embedding optimization equations remain unchanged. No new formal assumptions, mathematical derivations, theorems, or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: low-resource alignment through synthetic embeddings, applicability across three modalities, and VA-SafetyBench. The added analysis supports an existing rationale without redefining these central claims.

C2.justification: Appendix B.3 newly interprets style-dependent distributions as increased embedding diversity and suggests that fixed initialization explains LLaVA's default black-and-white style without style control. The existing limitations and main-result interpretations are retained.

D1.justification: V2 expands Figure 7 with worked intermediate examples, clarifies product-versus-activity targets and synthetic/real embedding integration, and adds scenario sample sizes to Tables 8–9. The abstract removes the promised code/data release URL. Hardware and alignment hyperparameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and related-work positioning are unchanged. The reference lists match after normalizing page breaks and hyphenation.

P1.justification: Sections 3.2, 3.4, and B.1 gain localized explanations, and the new B.3 moves the existing case-study subsection to B.4. Most prose and section organization are retained. Appendix A.3 introduces an unresolved 'Table X' reference.

P2.justification: V2 redraws the overview diagram, expands Figure 7, and adds Figure 8 and Table 11. Tables 8–9 gain sample-size columns, and Table 9 corrects copied video-task headings. Existing case-study figures are reformatted and renumbered; the overall document layout remains similar.

improvement.justification: The new style-control ablation supplies previously missing evidence for the diversity rationale, while expanded examples and sample-size reporting improve reproducibility. These gains are limited: the ablation does not assess downstream safety, the new video example contains a mismatched instruction, and v2 introduces 'Table X' while dropping the code/data release link. The added evidence and documentation provide a modest net improvement despite these regressions.
